source_ref: Jeon G-S, You S-J, Kim M-G, Kim Y-M, Cho S-I (2019) PLOS ONE 14(8):e0221323, 10.1371/journal.pone.0221323; S1 Fig (.s001, scanned CBI-K questionnaire, GIF) for the administered Korean wording and anchors; S2 File (.s002, SPSS .sav) variable labels and value labels; paper Results for the published subscale means
note: item codes ARE the source column names: data/jeon_2019_cbi_cesd.py melts the S2 .sav columns BT_I_1..6, BT_W_1..7, BT_C_1..6 straight through with no rename, so code->text needs no inference. The .sav's variable labels carry a terse English gloss of each item ('feel tired', 'end of the working day', 'give more than'); those were used for the MAPPING only. The WORDS shipped in item_text are the administered Korean, transcribed from S1 Fig, the scanned CBI-K questionnaire (GIF image -- OCR by eye, worth a human spot-check on the Korean orthography). All 19 labels line up 1:1 with the questionnaire's 6/7/6 layout in printed order. instructions = the form's header line; the three section_prompts are the form's own subscale headings. option_text = the five anchors printed across the form's column heads, matching the .sav's value labels ('alway(100%)'..'never(0%)'); data/jeon_2019_cbi_cesd.py maps never->0 .. alway->4. ANCHOR ORDER IS DELIBERATELY INVERTED FOR BT_W_4 ONLY: the deposited .sav already stores that item reverse-scored, so resp=4 there means the respondent ticked the 0% column, not the 100% one. Evidence: averaging the items as stored reproduces all three published subscale means exactly (PB 38.59/38.59, WRB 33.94/33.94, CRB 34.88/34.88, SDs 18.52/17.81/18.36 likewise); reversing BT_W_4 first would give WRB 36.12. BT_W_4's item-rest r as stored is +0.198, matching the paper's reported loading of +0.16/+0.19 for it -- a raw positively-worded 'do you have enough energy' item would correlate negatively. The English in the _translated columns was produced by this project from the Korean; it is NOT the canonical Kristensen et al. CBI wording, which the Korean form reorders and adapts ('service users and their guardians' rather than 'clients'). No rights restriction found: PLOS ONE is CC BY 4.0 and the CBI is distributed free of charge with no quotable fee or no-redistribution clause.
public_note: On BT_W_4 ('Do you have enough energy left to spend leisure time with friends or family?') the response scale runs the opposite way to the other 18 items: the deposited data already store this item reverse-scored, so resp=4 corresponds to the questionnaire's 0% anchor and resp=0 to its 100% anchor, and the shipped option_text reflects that. Averaging the items as stored reproduces the paper's published subscale means exactly (38.59 / 33.94 / 34.88); reversing BT_W_4 first would give 36.12 for the work-related subscale. The English _translated columns are IRW's own translation of the Korean questionnaire, not the authors' or the CBI publisher's.

source_ref: Jeon G-S, Suh S (2019) 'Sociodemographic and work-related factors associated with burnout among care workers in South Korea', PLOS ONE 14(8):e0221323, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0221323 (CC BY 4.0) -- Methods, 'Depressive symptoms' subsection; S2 File SPSS data doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0221323.s002 (variable and value labels for cesd1..cesd10, cached .cache/jeon_2019_cesd10/s002.sav); S1 Fig doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0221323.s001 (CBI-K questionnaire GIF, checked, contains no CESD-10). Processing script data/jeon_2019_cbi_cesd.py
note: Item text = the ten short English item descriptors the study itself publishes, taken from Jeon & Suh (2019) PLOS ONE 14(8):e0221323 Methods ('It consists of eight items addressing negative affect (loss of interest, trouble concentrating, feeling depressed, feeling tired or low in energy, feeling afraid, trouble falling asleep, feeling alone, and finding it hard to get going) and two items addressing positive affect (feel pretty good and generally satisfied)'), which reproduce the S2 File .sav's own variable labels for cesd1..cesd10. MAPPING: data/jeon_2019_cbi_cesd.py melts source columns cesd1..cesd10 by name (CESD_COLS = [f'cesd{i}' for i in range(1,11)]) with no rename, so the IRW item code IS the .sav column name and that column's variable label names its content -- 10/10 tied at the source, exempt derivation pattern 1. Independently corroborated: the paper's prose lists the eight negative descriptors in exactly cesd1,2,3,4,6,7,9,10 order and states the positive pair are 'items 5 and 8', matching labels cesd5 'feel pretty good' and cesd8 'generally satisfied'. DEVIATIONS FROM THE LABELS, all deliberate: cesd10 ships the paper's 'finding it hard to get going' rather than the .sav label's 'finding it hard to get along' (a typo; the canonical CES-D item is 'I could not get going'); cesd4 ships the paper's 'feeling tired or low in energy' rather than the label's 'tired or low in energy'; the anchors' en dashes are written as ASCII hyphens. Canonical Andresen CES-D-10 sentences were NOT substituted, because this version's item 1 is 'loss of interest' rather than canonical item 1 'bothered by things', so the two are not the same item set. OPTION TEXT / RESP DIRECTION: the paper states the coding outright ('0 = very rarely or less than once per day; 1 = sometimes or 1-2 days during the past week; 2 = often or 3-4 days during the past week; and 3 = almost always or 5-7 days during the past week') and this is exactly the label->integer MAP_CESD in the processing script. Verified against the published total: recoding the .sav by its value-label strings and reversing items 5 and 8 as the paper says it did reproduces the reported total mean 7.80 / SD 3.82 exactly (raw, unreversed, gives 6.06 / 4.39), so the live table stores the raw ascending-frequency direction shipped here. RIGHTS CHECKED, NO BLOCK: CES-D / CESD-10 has no quotable fee or no-redistribution clause; the shipped English is from a CC BY 4.0 article. LANGUAGE: administered in Korean; no Korean text in scope (S2 File .sav has zero Hangul across all 38 variable labels and all value labels; S1 Fig is the CBI-K questionnaire only; the article body prints none), so the English is the base text under the fallback. NOTE FOR THE SIBLING TABLE jeon_2019_cbi, not acted on here: the same .sav labels cover its BT_I_*/BT_W_*/BT_C_* columns and its S1 Fig IS a Korean CBI-K questionnaire image, so that table may be able to ship administered Korean where this one cannot.
public_note: The CESD-10 was administered to these Korean homecare workers in Korean, and no Korean wording is published in the article or either of its supporting files, so the text shown here is English. It is also not full item sentences: the study describes its ten items only as short phrases ('loss of interest', 'trouble concentrating', 'feel pretty good'), and those phrases are what ship, because this Korean short form's item 1 is 'loss of interest' rather than the canonical CES-D-10 item 1 and substituting the standard English sentences would have misrepresented the instrument. Items 5 and 8 are the positively worded ones and are stored unreversed in the response data, so the anchors shown apply as printed to every item

source_ref: Jiang et al. 2021, PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0245662 (CC BY 4.0); Table 4 (item wording prefixed with codes C1-C17) and Table 5 (per-item mean/SD); S4 File (.s004 DOCX) = the administered questionnaire, English and Chinese tables in identical order; S5 File (.s005 XLSX) = raw response data, header row 1 = C1..C17.
note: item_text is the Chinese wording respondents read, transcribed verbatim from the S4 File's Chinese questionnaire table; item_text_translated is the same document's own English table (study_supplied), not a translation by this project. Mapping is paper_explicit rather than data_labels: the S5 File header names the codes C1..C17 but carries no item text, while Table 4 prints each item prefixed with its own code ("C1 I am generally in good health." ... "C17 I can administer first aid."), so code->text is a label match for all 17. Two deliberate deviations, both literal-transcription departures: (1) for C14-C17 the questionnaire's second line ("Index illumination: ..." / "指标说明：...") is appended to the stem separated by a space rather than a newline, so each item ships as one field; Table 4 puts the same text in footnotes a-d with slightly different English (e.g. its footnote d reads "preliminary skills of first aid including performing hemostasis, applying bandages, administering CPR" where the questionnaire reads "preliminary skills of first aid including hemostasis, bandages, CPR") -- the questionnaire wording is what ships, since that is what respondents read. (2) internal newlines inside the DOCX table cells were collapsed to single spaces; nothing else altered. resp direction (5=完全符合/Extremely match ... 1=完全不符合/Extremely not match) is not stated in words anywhere, and was fixed numerically: per-item means computed from S5 under that reading land within 0.137 of the paper's Table 5 means on all 17 items, while the reversed reading is off by up to 3.047. Caveat: the deposit does not reproduce Table 5 exactly -- C14 3.51 vs 3.65 and C17 3.22 vs 3.36 are the worst, and the paper's claim that C3 and C12 have SD<0.75 reproduces for C3 (0.695) but not C12 (0.763, while C2 is 0.745); the ordering is unaffected. No rights restriction found on the wording: the instrument was constructed by these authors and published in full in their own CC BY 4.0 article and its S4 File.
